english.note: Use this as the all-purpose colloquial choice for “about,” especially for approximate degree or comparison such as “about as cold.”
This is the all-purpose spoken choice for being nearly at a state or for nearly all or no people or things.
This is the all-purpose choice for saying that something is nearly or almost at a stated degree or condition.
Use this for “almost completely,” especially when describing extent or quantity.
This is the all-purpose choice for “almost” or “nearly,” including approximate amounts such as nearly two hours.
This is the all-purpose spoken choice for “nearly” or “almost,” including “almost unconscious.”
Use this colloquial alternative when the amount is roughly the stated figure rather than exact.
Use 差唔多 as the all-purpose spoken choice for “almost” or “nearly.”
Choose this when basically means pretty much or more or less, rather than fundamentally.
